name: South Mumbai Heritage Walk by MDT
description:
The Mumbai Heritage Walk is a great way to experience the city’s vibrant culture and rich history.
Mumbai Heritage Walk is probably known as the ‘dream city’ and rightly so the city is indeed like a beautiful, magnificent dream. Old Mumbai is the part of Mumbai that represents its heritage and history. Reflecting on the time of Colonial era, the area is studded with numerous tourist attractions. From Chhatrapati Shivaji terminus to the ‘White town’ to the University library to the magnificent Marine drive, the city has so many spectacular attractions that one can never miss. Explore all these places of Old Mumbai and many more with this heritage walk tour.

Walking tours expose many residents and visitors to the structures.

customer_updates.text:
Nestled majestically beside the Sabarmati River at the foot of Ellis Bridge in Ahmedabad lies the historic Lokmanya Tilak Garden, formerly Victoria Garden (est. 1905). Spanning over 28,260 m², this greenscape is a serene blend of regal heritage and modern charm—perfect for your next share! 🌿

🕰️ Timeless Origins
Built to commemorate Queen Victoria’s Diamond Jubilee, the garden opened its gates in 1905 and became one of India’s earliest urban parks  . Over time, it embraced its patriotic identity, honoring freedom fighters through stately monuments.

🎖️ Monuments with Meaning

A striking bronze statue of Lokmanya Tilak, unveiled by Gandhi in 1929, stands tall, bearing his famous motto **“Swarajya is my birth‑right”**  .

The Mahagujarat Shaheed Smarak commemorates brave students of the 1956 language movement  .

Ornate vestiges like the Queen Victoria canopy, Nanavatty fountain, and more enrich the grounds with layers of history  .

🌳 Garden Features
Today’s revamped space (redeveloped in 2021 with a ₹10 crore facelift) offers:

Wide walkways, manicured lawns, and a restored bandstand

A calming forest-walk, maze garden, children’s play area, jogging trails, fountains, and convenient amenities

📅 Visitor Info
Open 6 AM–12:30 PM, then 2 PM–10:30 PM daily. It welcomed over 10 lakh visitors in 2023 and continues to shine under city beautification awards  .

featured_reviews.review_text:

There is no entry ticket, making it easily accessible to everyone. However, the garden lacks proper maintenance, and it could definitely be better looked after to enhance the overall experience.

Overall, it’s a simple place to spend a short amount of time, mainly because of its greenery and seaside location, but improved maintenance would make it much better.
